correctness.rationale: For general three-dimensional polytopes, projection domination follows from Kiderlen Theorem 1.2 and Cauchy. The explicit even spherical polynomial g vanishes at every atom of the Blaschke surface measure. All even Legendre cosine eigenvalues through degree 2m are nonzero, with exact factorial formula checked by independent exact-rational recurrence. Spherical projectors and |P_l|<=1 bound the finite inverse q in sup norm, making the density 1/(2pi)-epsilon*q positive. Integrating yields epsilon*int g dmu<=2delta. Separation of distinct projective facet-normal lines gives g>=rho^2 sin(Delta/2)^(2m-2). Explicit facet splitting preserves every projection inequality and proves the optimal angular exponent. No numerical finite test is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural quantitative gap in the 2026 universal polytope weak-barrier theory is whether each fixed spatial polytope permits a linear Jones-deficit angular concentration estimate. The proof gives an explicit uniform finite-facet certificate without central symmetry, stronger integrated squared-angle control, and a constructive proof that the angular denominator power 2 cannot be reduced for weak barriers. It is not a routine parameter substitution from the cube, whose proof relies on coordinate Rademacher symmetry.
